question: The height, h, in metres, that the ladder reaches up the wall is
stem: The height, h, in metres, that the ladder reaches up the wall is

misconception.label: Used the sine ratio
misconception.remediation_hint: Sine needs the hypotenuse, but the 5 m is the side ADJACENT to the angle.

misconception.label: Used the cosine ratio
misconception.remediation_hint: Cosine would give a length shorter than 5 m, but the wall is taller than that.

misconception.label: Found the length of the ladder instead of the height
misconception.remediation_hint: That gives the hypotenuse, not the height up the wall.

worked_solution: Relative to the 62 degree angle, the 5 m is the ADJACENT side and h is the OPPOSITE side. tan 62 = opposite / adjacent = h / 5. h = 5 tan 62 degrees.
hints: Sine needs the hypotenuse, but the 5 m is the side ADJACENT to the angle.
Cosine would give a length shorter than 5 m, but the wall is taller than that.
That gives the hypotenuse, not the height up the wall.
common_mistakes: Found the length of the ladder instead of the height
learning_objective: Choose the correct trigonometric ratio in a right-angled triangle.
exam_skill: Match the given and required sides to the correct ratio
